chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Abbas ibn Al-Walid ibn Sabih, who said:

Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih asked me to seek permission for him from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). So I informed Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) of this, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Tell him to come to us whenever he wishes.' So I brought him in to him at night, and Shihab was wearing a head covering. A cushion was placed for him, so he sat on it. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Remove your veil, O Shihab, for the veil is a source of doubt (or suspicion) by night and a sign of humility (or disgrace) by day.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of removing the head covering (qina') according to Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) instructs Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih to remove his head covering (*qina'*) during a night audience, explaining that it causes suspicion (*ribah*) at night due to obscured identity, while signifying humility (*madhallah*) by day. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of social etiquette and the importance of transparency in personal interactions, distinguishing between modesty and concealment based on context and time.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Abbas Bin Al Waleed Bin Sabeeh who said,

‘Shihab Bin Abd Rabih asked me that I should seek permission for him to (see) Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>. So I let Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> know about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Tell him he can come to us<sup>asws</sup> whenever he so desires to’. So I took him over to him<sup>asws</sup> one night, and Shihab wore a covering of the head. I placed a cushion for him, so he sat over it and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Remove you veil O Shihab, for the veil casts a doubt during the night and is a disgrace during the day’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn Mahbub from al-‘ Ab has ibn al-Walid ibn Sabiyh who has said the following:

“Once Shihab ibn ‘ Abd Rabbihi asked me to ask permission for him to visit abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and I informed him (the Imam) about it. He (the Imam) said, ’He can visit if he likes.’ I took him to the house of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. It was during the night and Shihab had a mask on him. I found a furnishing for him to sit on and he sat down. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, said to him, ‘O Shihab, remove your mask; it causes doubt during the night and disgrace in the day.’”
